question: Which type of lung cancer is the most commonly diagnosed in clinical practice?
explanation: You've got this! Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer accounts for about 85% of all lung cancer cases, making it much more common than the small cell type. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is Small Cell Lung Cancer usually treated with medications (systemic therapy) rather than surgery right away?

options.A: It only occurs in patients who are too old for operations.
options.B: It grows extremely slowly inside the main bronchial tubes.
options.C: It usually spreads to other body parts very early before detection.
options.D: It is completely resistant to any form of surgical removal.

explanation: Great thinking! Small cell lung cancer grows fast and tends to spread (metastasize) early, meaning surgery alone usually isn't enough to catch it all. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: After cigarette smoking, what is recognized as the second leading cause of lung cancer?
explanation: Spot on! Radon is a natural radioactive gas that can build up in buildings. After smoking, it's the next big culprit behind lung cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: A patient who has never smoked in their life develops lung cancer. Which workplace exposure is a very likely culprit?
explanation: Well done! Breathing in asbestos dust on the job is a well-known risk factor that can cause severe lung damage and cancer, even in non-smokers. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is usually the first sign that makes a patient say, 'I need to get this cough checked out'?
explanation: Exactly! A new cough that just won't go away is the most common early warning sign of a lung issue. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why do many lung cancer patients only discover they are sick when the disease is already advanced?

options.A: The lungs lack pain receptors, allowing tumors to grow undetected initially.
options.B: Symptoms only appear after the cancer completely destroys the heart.
options.C: Early lung tumors cause immediate total paralysis of the limbs.
options.D: Blood tests detect the cancer cells only during late stages.

explanation: You got it! Because lung tissue doesn't have pain nerve endings, a small tumor can grow quietly for a long time without causing any physical pain. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which test gives doctors the final, definitive confirmation that a patient has lung cancer?
explanation: Spot on! Scans can strongly suggest cancer, but a pathologist needs to look at an actual tissue sample under a microscope to confirm it. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using the TNM staging system for lung cancer?

options.A: To determine the extent of disease spread and plan appropriate treatment
options.B: To measure the exact volume of air the lungs can hold
options.C: To calculate the patient's exact daily calorie requirements
options.D: To identify which specific type of cigarette the patient smoked

explanation: Brilliant! TNM helps the team figure out how big the tumor is, if it has reached lymph nodes, and how far it has spread, guiding the best treatment plan. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the main goal when a patient is caught early with non-small cell lung cancer?
explanation: You're doing great! If the cancer is caught early and hasn't spread, cutting out the tumor surgically gives the best chance for a complete cure. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h5)

question: How does immunotherapy work differently from standard chemotherapy?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any diagnostic imaging procedures.
options.B: It only acts on the outer layer of the skin and never reaches the lungs.
options.C: It freezes the tumor tissue by lowering the core body temperature.
options.D: It empowers the body's own immune defenses to target and destroy cancer cells.

explanation: Exactly right! Instead of just attacking cells directly like chemo, immunotherapy helps your own white blood cells recognize and fight off the cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is the quickest way to help a patient who is suddenly struggling to catch their breath due to lung cancer?

options.A: Laying the patient flat on their back in bed
options.B: Placing the patient in a high-Fowler's position
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake for twelve hours

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Sitting the patient upright in a high-Fowler's position lets their chest expand fully, making it much easier to draw breath. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: A patient who just had lung surgery is scared to cough because their incision hurts. What should you, the nurse, do first?

options.A: Tell the patient that coughing is optional and let them sleep all day.
options.B: Apply a tight chest binder to completely immobilize the chest wall.
options.C: Administer prescribed pain medication before encouraging controlled coughing exercises.
options.D: Report the patient immediately to the surgeon for emergency re-operation.

explanation: Wonderful clinical judgment! Controlling the pain first allows the patient to cough and clear their lungs safely without agony, preventing complications like collapsed lung areas. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which screening tool is best for catching lung cancer early in high-risk people who don't have symptoms yet?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain

explanation: You've got this! A low-dose CT scan captures clear images of the lungs using very low radiation, making it the gold standard for high-risk screening. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why is quitting smoking considered 'primary prevention' rather than 'secondary prevention'?

options.A: It is only performed after a patient receives a confirmed cancer diagnosis.
options.B: It relies entirely on surgical removal of damaged bronchial tissue.
options.C: It focuses on finding small tumors before symptoms appear.
options.D: It aims to prevent the disease from ever developing in the first place.

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops harmful exposures (like tobacco) so the disease process never even gets a chance to start. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)
